title: What he loved in a big band's sound
summary: He loved the saxophones, trumpets, trombones and tuba, disliked clarinet's squeak, and his mother saw he would stay with drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Hanging around bands like that, were there -- which horns and whatnot, which pleased you? I mean, did you love to hear the brass, or did you love to hear the saxophones?
I loved to hear the saxophone and the trumpet and the trombone, and the clarinet I didn't care too much for the clarinet. It was too, like, squeaky for me.
Yeah, didn't have that forceful --
No, you know.
It's like embroidery.
But the trombone, the trumpet and saxophone, I liked.
Yeah. You liked the tenor, particularly.
Yeah, right. It was heavier.
Yeah, that's right.
And they would have a tuba player, even, you know.
Oh, yeah, yeah.
I liked that.
Yeah. People had begun to use string bass by then, hadn't they?
Yes, they were using it.
They were just beginning to.
They were beginning to use the string bass a lot. But they used mostly the tuba, one of those things.
Right.
And just to hear the band tune up knocked me out. I enjoyed that. That's the way it was with me.
Yeah, yeah, it's your love, the love of your life, yeah.
Yeah.
So did your mother, -- she began to realize by then, did she realize that you were going to turn out to be a musician? Did she suspect you were?
I don't think that she really knew that I would be a musician. But she knew I loved music. One of those things.
Yeah.
And then, when I stuck with the drums,
well, that was it.
Yeah, that you were going to be a drummer.
